question: Which stock entry points back battery state, wake locks, screen state/wake, manual brightness, vibration and system properties for the Supervisor platform services?
prototype_hypothesis: Stock PowerManager/MiWearScreen/vibrator/property APIs are called as ordinary AAPCS functions from the UI owner thread; none is ISR-safe.
callsite_evidence: PowerManager wakelock_create accepts only level 6 and 26 (invalid levelAndFlags log); the stock alarm and sport apps use it as a screen keep-on lock.
MiWearScreen __func__ strings screen_turn_on, screen_session_{create,start,stop,set_brightness_value,set_auto_brightness,restore_default} each map to one function through string cross-references.
Stock brightness: apply_brightness_settings arbitrates active sessions; the user setting clamps to 31..255 and persists as persist.screen.brightness_value.
Bluetooth adapter state compares against 0 (off) and 4 (on) in stock code; bt_adapter_get_state is already a recovered symbol.

system_state.c update_from_bt_state writes state[1] = 2 when the MiWear connection is up (else 1) and state[2] = 2 when the Bluetooth ACL is up (else 1); the control-center status bar shows phone_conn.bin for 2 and phone_disconn.bin for 0, so 0 means not yet reported.
control_flow_evidence: exact 4.100.139 IDB vela_ap.bin.i64; body shape identical to the reviewed 4.100.155 function and unique in this image
ownership_analysis: wakelock and screen session objects are heap objects owned by the creator; the Supervisor creates a bounded set once and never destroys them, so no free path is called. Tag strings passed to create calls must outlive the objects (static storage in the Supervisor).
unsafe_assumptions: No device probe: argument registers, blocking behavior and thread affinity are inferred from decompilation only.
Brightness override relies on session arbitration; stock UI may overwrite it when the user changes brightness.
recommended_probe: Mirage or device: query battery, toggle a Canopus wakelock with the screen idle, set brightness to 20% and 100%, vibrate 50 ms and cancel.
